faq.q: Is City Index legit or a scam?
faq.a: City Index is one of the most legitimate brokers in existence. Founded in London in 1983, regulated by the FCA (licence 446717), ASIC, MAS, and five other global regulators, and owned by NASDAQ-listed StoneX Group. UK clients receive FSCS protection up to GBP 85,000. City Index has operated continuously for over 41 years without a single regulatory scandal.

faq.q: What is City Index minimum deposit?
faq.a: City Index requires a minimum deposit of £100 for UK clients and $150 for Australian and Singapore clients. Singapore clients funding via credit card have a $250 minimum per card transaction. The Premium account tier requires £10,000 for access to tighter pricing.

faq.q: How long do City Index withdrawals take?
faq.a: City Index withdrawals via debit card or PayPal are typically processed same day. Bank wire transfers take 1-3 business days. There are no withdrawal fees. You must withdraw to the same method used for deposit up to the deposited amount — standard anti-money-laundering procedure.

faq.q: Is City Index spread betting tax-free?
faq.a: Yes — for UK residents, spread betting profits with City Index are free from capital gains tax and stamp duty under current HMRC rules. This is a genuine financial advantage over CFD trading where profits are taxable. Tax laws may change and depend on individual circumstances.

faq.q: What platforms does City Index offer?
faq.a: City Index offers four platforms: their proprietary Web Trader (award-winning, 90+ indicators), MetaTrader 4, TradingView integration for direct chart execution, and a dedicated mobile app. Web Trader is the flagship platform with customisable workspaces and advanced charting.

faq.q: What are City Index spreads on EUR/USD?
faq.a: City Index Standard accounts average 0.5 pips on EUR/USD with no commission — all-in cost of approximately $5 per standard lot. Premium accounts (£10,000 minimum) access tighter pricing from 0.3 pips. Pricing is spread-only with no separate commission structure.

faq.q: Does City Index charge an inactivity fee?
faq.a: Yes — City Index charges a £12 monthly inactivity fee after 12 consecutive months of no trading activity. You can avoid this by placing at least one trade within any 12-month period, or by closing your account if you do not intend to trade. The fee only applies to funded accounts.

City Index is owned by StoneX Group Inc (NASDAQ: SNEX), a Fortune 500 financial services company. StoneX acquired City Index through its 2020 acquisition of GAIN Capital. This institutional backing provides financial stability that standalone brokers cannot match.

sections.heading: Is City Index Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Forty-one years of continuous operation without a regulatory scandal. FCA regulated. ASIC regulated. MAS regulated. Backed by a NASDAQ-listed parent company worth billions. And still offering a £100 minimum deposit that makes institutional-grade safety accessible to retail traders who are not sitting on a trust fund. City Index is not the flashiest broker in the market — it is the one your money is safest at. Execution averages 20 milliseconds. The Web Trader platform genuinely competes with anything the boutique fintechs are shipping. And for UK residents, tax-free spread betting means your profits stay yours.

But — and this matters — City Index is not the cheapest. Standard spreads start at 0.5 pips EUR/USD. That is fair, not exceptional. ECN brokers like IC Markets or Pepperstone will give you raw pricing from 0.0 pips at lower all-in cost. The £12 monthly inactivity fee catches casual traders who forget about dormant accounts. And Premium tier pricing — where spreads drop to 0.3 pips — requires £10,000 sitting in your account.

This broker is built for active UK and Australian traders who want to know — genuinely know — that their capital is safe, their fills are fast, and their counterparty will still exist next decade.

sections.heading: Is City Index Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Emphatically yes — and at the highest tier available. StoneX Financial Ltd (trading as City Index) holds FCA authorisation number 446717, which means full compliance with the UK's most stringent financial conduct rules. UK retail clients receive FSCS protection up to GBP 85,000 per person if the broker becomes insolvent. Your money is held in segregated accounts at major UK banks, separate from the company's operational funds.

In Australia, StoneX Financial Pty Ltd operates under ASIC licence 345646 with equivalent segregation requirements. No investor compensation scheme exists under ASIC — but fund segregation applies. Singapore clients are covered by the MAS-regulated entity (CMS100631) with client money protection rules. Additional licences cover UAE (CBUAE), Canada (CIRO), Cyprus (CySEC), Japan (FSA), and Hong Kong (SFC).

One note worth tracking: Gain Capital UK — the former parent entity associated with both City Index and Forex.com — announced plans to surrender its separate FCA licence. This does not affect City Index, which continues operating under StoneX Financial Ltd's own FCA authorisation. But it signals corporate restructuring that traders should monitor. The StoneX Group parent (NASDAQ: SNEX) reported over $60 billion in client assets across its divisions — this is not a company at risk of disappearing overnight.

sections.heading: Who Can Open an Account With City Index? — Accepted Countries and Restrictions
sections.body:
Accepted: United Kingdom, Australia, Singapore, United Arab Emirates, Canada, Hong Kong, Japan, Cyprus, New Zealand, and select EEA countries.

Not accepted: United States (served under the Forex.com brand instead), India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, most of Africa, most of Southeast Asia (excluding Singapore), North Korea, Iran, Syria, Cuba, Crimea, Russia, Myanmar.

City Index is not a broker that accepts everyone. Unlike offshore operations that onboard clients from 190+ countries, City Index only operates where it holds specific regulatory authorisation. If your country is not on the accepted list, you genuinely cannot open an account — there is no backdoor entity routing through an offshore jurisdiction. This is a feature, not a limitation. It means every client has regulatory recourse in their home jurisdiction.
sections.practical_note: UK residents get the best deal — FCA protection plus tax-free spread betting. Australian residents get ASIC oversight but no tax advantage on spread bets (not available in AU). Singapore residents face slightly higher minimum deposits ($150 standard, $250 via card). If you are outside these core markets, City Index may not be accessible to you.

sections.heading: City Index Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
Standard accounts give you 0.5 pips average on EUR/USD with zero commission. All-in cost per round-turn standard lot: approximately $5.00. That is competitive for a Tier-1 FCA broker but not market-leading — Pepperstone Razor at 0.0 + $7 commission often works out cheaper on high-frequency strategies. Where City Index earns back the difference is on indices and commodities, where spreads are genuinely tight — UK100 from 0.8 points, Wall Street from 1.0 point.

Premium accounts unlock tighter forex pricing at 0.3 pips EUR/USD average — but require £10,000 minimum equity. That is a real barrier for most retail traders. The MT4 account mirrors Standard pricing and is available for traders who prefer MetaTrader's infrastructure over the proprietary platform.

Hidden costs to watch: overnight funding charges of 2.5% plus the relevant benchmark rate compound quickly on positions held for days or weeks. A £10,000 position on UK100 held overnight costs roughly £0.68 per night at current rates — that adds up to £20+ per month if you are swing trading. The £12 monthly inactivity fee after 12 months catches anyone who opens an account and forgets about it. No deposit or withdrawal fees — a genuine positive that some competitors cannot match. Spread betting in the UK is commission-free by definition, with costs embedded entirely in the spread.

table.footnote: Spread data is broker-stated average for EUR/USD. Overnight funding of 2.5% + benchmark rate applies to all positions held past market close. Professional clients may access 1:200 leverage upon qualification.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of City Index?
sections.body:
Zero fees on both deposits and withdrawals — across all methods. That is the headline and it matters. No $5 flat fee, no percentage charge, no hidden processing cost. Your money moves for free.

Deposits via debit card are instant. Bank wire takes 1-3 business days. PayPal is instant. No credit card funding accepted — this is an FCA compliance choice that actually protects you from funding leveraged trading with borrowed money.

Withdrawals process same-day for card and PayPal when requested before the cut-off time. Bank wire withdrawals take 1-3 business days after City Index processes the request. The standard anti-money-laundering rule applies — you must withdraw to the same method used for deposit up to the deposited amount. Profits above deposit amount can route to bank wire. Minimum withdrawal applies based on method.

table.footnote: No credit cards accepted for deposits. All withdrawal fees are $0. Processing times based on requests before internal cut-off (broker-stated).

sections.heading: City Index Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Trustpilot shows City Index at approximately 4.2 out of 5 from around 850 reviews — solid but not exceptional for a broker this size. Review velocity is moderate at 15-25 per month, consistent with an established UK brand that does not aggressively solicit reviews. Positive feedback centres on platform reliability and execution speed. Negative reviews cluster around two themes: unexpected overnight funding charges on positions held longer than intended, and the inactivity fee catching dormant account holders.

The positive pattern: withdrawals are generally clean and predictable. Multiple public reports confirm standard withdrawals processing same-day for card and PayPal. Traders consistently report that funds appear within 1-2 business days for card refunds after City Index releases the payment. No withdrawal fees means no nasty surprise at the exit — a genuine differentiator against brokers charging $5-$25 per withdrawal.

The complaint pattern: very few withdrawal-specific complaints compared to the broader market. The complaints that exist tend to relate to margin close-outs during volatile sessions (which is market risk, not broker misconduct) or confusion about the anti-money-laundering requirement to withdraw to the original deposit method. Nothing in the public record suggests systematic withdrawal obstruction or delay tactics.

If a withdrawal stalls: contact live chat first (fastest response channel per the broker). Escalate via formal written complaint to Moor House, 120 London Wall, London EC2Y 5ET. UK clients can escalate further to the Financial Ombudsman Service — this is the FCA advantage. NAFT maintains a complaints portal at /complaints for documented withdrawal issues.

sections.heading: City Index Red Flags — What to Know Before You Deposit
sections.body: No major red flags. City Index has operated for 41 years under FCA oversight without a significant regulatory enforcement action. The NASDAQ-listed parent provides financial transparency through public quarterly filings. That said, a few items deserve attention before you commit capital — not because they signal fraud, but because they affect your bottom line. The Gain Capital UK FCA licence surrender announcement is corporate housekeeping, not a warning — but traders should monitor StoneX announcements for any structural changes to the City Index entity itself. sections.heading: Who Should Use City Index — and Who Should Not
sections.body: City Index is a broker that knows exactly who it is for — and is not trying to be everything to everyone. The restricted geographic access is the clearest signal. If you can open an account here, you are getting one of the safest counterparties available in retail trading.
not_for: Cost-sensitive scalpers — at 0.5 pips EUR/USD on Standard, you are paying more than ECN brokers offering 0.0 pips. If every tenth of a pip matters to your edge, go to IC Markets or Pepperstone
Traders outside UK, Australia, Singapore, UAE, and Canada — City Index simply does not accept you. No workaround, no offshore entity backdoor

Beginners with under £500 — the platform is powerful but complex, overnight funding compounds quickly on small accounts, and the 1:30 retail leverage means you need adequate capital to take meaningful positions
Swing traders who hold positions for weeks — overnight funding at 2.5% + benchmark rate will erode returns on any position held longer than a few days

sections.heading: How to Open a City Index Account — Step by Step
sections.body: Registration takes under five minutes online. Verification is typically same-day for UK residents with valid photo ID. The process is straightforward for anyone who has opened a financial account before.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit cityindex.com and select your region (UK, AU, or SG). Click 'Create Account' and complete the application form — personal details, employment status, trading experience. Select spread betting or CFD account (UK), or CFD account (AU/SG). The whole form takes under 5 minutes.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload government-issued photo ID (passport or driving licence) and proof of address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months). UK residents can use electronic verification for faster processing. Verification typically completes same-day during business hours.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit minimum £100 via debit card or PayPal (instant) or bank wire (1-3 days). Place one trade to test execution speed and spreads. Then request a small withdrawal to verify the process — zero fees, same-day processing on card and PayPal. Confirm everything works before committing serious capital.

sections.practical_note: Make a small deposit. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately. If it processes cleanly, scale with confidence. If anything feels wrong at any step, do not deposit more.

sections.heading: City Index Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores City Index 8.4 out of 10. Eight regulatory licences across three continents. A 41-year operating history without a single major enforcement action. FSCS protection for UK clients. Zero withdrawal fees. And a NASDAQ-listed parent whose quarterly filings are public record. This is about as safe as retail trading gets — and execution quality at 20ms average means you are not sacrificing performance for safety.

The cost is not being the cheapest. Standard spreads at 0.5 pips EUR/USD are fair but not exceptional. The £12 inactivity fee is an irritation. Overnight funding charges punish anyone who uses this as a swing trading account rather than a day trading one. And if you are outside the UK, Australia, or Singapore, you simply cannot access this broker — there is no offshore backdoor.

For UK residents specifically, NAFT considers City Index one of the strongest options available. Tax-free spread betting, FCA protection, institutional execution, and a platform that has quietly become excellent. If you want the cheapest possible all-in cost, look at Pepperstone Razor. If you want the safest counterparty with genuinely good execution and you live in the UK — City Index earns its place on your shortlist.
